previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted due to dizziness, nausea, leg weakness, and imbalance, initially concerning for stroke. She was last known well at 10:00 a.m. on the day of admission. Evaluation revealed no acute stroke on CT or MRI of the brain. Her symptoms were attributed to peripheral vestibulopathy, likely triggered by metabolic disturbances including hyperkalemia (K+ 6.4). She underwent four hemodialysis sessions during admission, with improvement in electrolyte levels and symptom resolution. She experienced an episode of hypotension during one dialysis session, which resolved with fluid administration and machine recalibration. Meclizine was prescribed for persistent dizziness, and outpatient physical therapy was arranged for balance training. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications, including increased omeprazole and amlodipine, and instructions to continue dialysis and follow up with neurology and hematology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with PMHx lupus, anti-phospholipid antibody syndrome, and 
ESRD  s/p failed transplant on HD MWF, who presented to the ED 
today with dizziness, unsteady gait and confusion. She was 
dialyzed with resolution of her hyperkalemia. Dizziness and 
unsteadiness also resolved without clear cause identified, but 
most likely related to atypical migraine. 

Active Issues:

# Hyperkalemia
Potassium on admission 7.0. No clear acute etiology - no 
medication changes, compliant with HD schedule, complaint with 
diet. ECG with associated peaked-T waves. She was dialyzed with 
resolution. She was continued on home kayexalate 3x/week. 

# Dizziness, unsteadiness
Patient has history of intermittent dizziness episodes. She is 
followed by neurology and thought to have migraine equivalent. 
CT head negative for acute process. No clear evidence of 
arrhythmia, vestibulopathy, and no CVA/TIA symptomatology. 
Neurologic exam was normal. Her symptoms resolved spontaneously, 
and she was asymptomatic with ambulation. This was felt to be an 
acute exacerbation of a chronic issue.

# Confusion
Patient presented with difficulty performing tasks such as 
programming thermostat and typing. No clear acute etiology and 
head CT was negative. ___ be secondary to on-going cognitive 
decline. Mental status exam was intact on discharge. ___ benefit 
from formal cognitive testing in the future. 

Chronic Issues:

# ESRD
Secondary to thrombotic microangiopathy s/p failed transplant, 
on HD three times a week. Received dialysis prior to admission.

#HTN
Continued on home amlodipine and labetolol.

#APLA
Continued on home warfarin 3mg daily with goal INR 1.5-2.5 per 
patient. INR at discharge was therapeutic at 1.8.

Transitional Issues:
1. Tranaminitis and episodic epigastric pain - has been noted up 
as an outpatient with plans for MRCP. LFTs checked on admission 
were downtrending from outpatient labs and she had no pain; MRCP 
not able to be done on day of discharge, deferred to outpatient. 

2. ___ benefit from formal cognitive testing given her concerns 
for decreased executive functioning. 
3. Noted to have mild leukopenia and thrombocytopenia. PCP aware 
on discharge and should recheck at post-discharge follow-up. 
4. Full Code

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History: ___ with dizziness  // stroke

TECHNIQUE:  Routine unenhanced head CT was performed and viewed in brain,
intermediate and bone windows.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were also
performed.

DOSE:  DLP:  892 mGy-cm
CTDI:  55 mGy

COMPARISON:  Nonenhanced head CT dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, acute major vascular territorial
infarction, edema or mass effect. Mild prominence of ventricles and sulci is
compatible with age related involutional changes. The basal cisterns are
clear.  The gray white matter differentiation appears preserved.  No fracture
is identified.  Mild mucosal thickening is noted within the right sphenoid
sinus. The remainder the visualized paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and
middle ear cavities are clear. Incidental note is made of vascular
calcifications within the carotid siphons.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute intracranial abnormality.
